title: Matcha White Chocolate Chip Cookies
story: The matcha makes these green. Not hint-of-green, properly green, in a way that makes people either excited or suspicious depending on the person. Use good matcha; the cheap stuff tastes like a lawn and turns the cookies a color that requires explanation. The white chocolate is there for contrast, and the contrast works.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature

steps.text: Sift 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp matcha powder, and ½ tsp fine salt into a medium bowl. Sifting the matcha prevents green clumps in the finished cookie.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter, ½ cup granulated sugar, and ½ cup packed brown sugar together until light and creamy, about 2–3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look noticeably paler and fluffy — this builds the cookie's structure.

steps.text: Beat in 1 large egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract until fully combined.
Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain.
Fold in 1 cup white chocolate chips.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.

steps.donenessCue: The matcha color makes the tops unreliable — watch the edges instead. They should look just set and dry at the rim while the centers still look soft. They'll firm up as they cool.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while still warm if using.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Chill the dough for 30 minutes before baking — the cookies spread less and the matcha flavor deepens.
Use ceremonial-grade matcha for a more vivid green color and a cleaner, less bitter flavor. Culinary grade works but the color will be duller.
Swap the chips for roughly chopped white chocolate — the irregular pieces melt into better puddles.
Add ¼ tsp almond extract alongside the vanilla for a subtle richness that plays well with the matcha.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Freeze unbaked dough balls for up to 3 months — bake from frozen at 350°F, adding 2–3 minutes to the bake time.
